reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides customer-support guidance for an eBay buyer who has not received an item, including checking the estimated delivery date and contacting the seller. It concerns an existing purchase dispute and suggests requesting a refund or the item and escalating to eBay, rather than soliciting an investment, payment, credentials, or other participation from viewers. The described material supports an ordinary support and dispute-resolution context, although the operation or outcome of any external service is not independently established.

citations.quote: As a buyer on eBay, if you haven't received your item this video is intended to help.
We will show you how to verify the estimated delivery date, how to reach out to your seller and if needs be, open up a case.
So the first thing you want to do if you believe your item is going to be late is check your estimated delivery date.
if the item is beyond the delivery date and you haven't received your items you can let the seller know by opening a request
You can then add a custom message to the request to let your seller know any additional details, then select send request.

opening.argument: The video links a potential return of the buyer's money to a concrete sequence of viewer actions: checking delivery details, contacting the seller, and sending a request. That is more than general information; it presents an easy recovery pathway whose benefit depends on using the platform's prescribed flow. The viewer is also directed toward an external customer-service contact, extending the action pathway beyond the video itself. The promised outcome is not independently demonstrated, but the combination of a claimed refund option and a low-effort request process is sufficient to warrant treating this as a solicitation for participation in a return flow.

citations.quote: you can ask eBay to step in
selecting either, I want a refund or I want the item
For help outside these hours, please contact eBay Customer Service at http://ebay.to/2elcv5C

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this dispute resolution, but that characterization does not remove the solicitation. Viewers are told to choose a desired outcome and send a custom request, then escalate if dissatisfied. The fact that the subject begins with a missing purchase does not establish that the advertised recovery process will work, and the defense supplies no evidence that any refund or intervention actually occurred.

citations.quote: You can then add a custom message to the request to let your seller know any additional details, then select send request.
If you're not satisfied with the resolution the seller provides you can ask eBay to step in.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted actions do not show a low-barrier reward scheme. They describe a buyer addressing an existing transaction, and the video expressly conditions the request on the item being beyond its delivery date. A choice between wanting the item and requesting a refund is not evidence that money is promised to viewers generally, and no payment, fee, credential request, or guaranteed outcome is shown.

citations.quote: If the date hasn't passed, then the item may still be in transit.
if the item is beyond the delivery date and you haven't received your items
As a buyer on eBay, if you haven't received your item this video is intended to help.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an off-platform-looking customer-service URL, a narrow support window that creates a reason to use that link, and a strongly reassuring money-back statement. The process also sets short resolution timelines, which can make the viewer act quickly rather than independently verify the service. These signals surround an easy claim process involving a refund or further intervention. Even if each item can be given an ordinary explanation, their combination presents a polished, confidence-building recovery funnel whose actual operation and outcome are not established by the video.

citations.quote: eBay YouTube Customer Support Hours are Monday – Friday, 6:00AM – 6:00PM PST.
please contact eBay Customer Service at http://ebay.to/2elcv5C
this seller has four business days to resolve it
I personally love the eBay Money-back guarantee because it makes me feel very safe purchasing on the website.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the link and deadlines ordinary support features overlooks how they function persuasively: they create urgency, provide a designated contact route, and end with a personal safety endorsement. The defense identifies the subject matter but does not verify the linked destination, the guarantee's applicability, or whether the stated deadlines produce the claimed result. Those omissions matter when the presentation asks viewers to rely on the process.

citations.quote: For help outside these hours, please contact eBay Customer Service at http://ebay.to/2elcv5C
get back with you within two business days

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not presented as unexplained benefits or urgent payments. The timing is tied to a seller's response and eBay's review of a specific request, while the support hours simply describe when help is available. The video never claims that every viewer receives money, and its reassurance does not establish deception or a fabricated result.

citations.quote: we will review your request to see if it qualifies for a eBay Money-back guarantee
Once you've opened a request this seller has four business days to resolve it
As a buyer on eBay, if you haven't received your item this video is intended to help.

opening.argument: Although framed as support, the presentation also promotes continued participation in eBay's transaction and dispute system. The speaker identifies herself as customer service, appears in branded eBay clothing, and walks viewers through contacting sellers, submitting a request, selecting a refund, and asking eBay to intervene. The closing endorsement that the guarantee feels safe purchasing on the website reinforces the commercial relationship rather than neutrally documenting a problem. This framing can steer viewers toward the platform's recovery funnel while presenting the result as routine and dependable, even though the video does not establish the external service's operation or any successful outcome.

citations.quote: I'm Kim, I work for eBay's customer service
I personally love the eBay Money-back guarantee because it makes me feel very safe purchasing on the website.
you can ask eBay to step in

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the branded setting as proof of ordinary support, but branding is precisely what makes the guidance promotional: it lends authority to a process that directs viewers to contact sellers, submit requests, and seek a refund or intervention. The endorsement of purchasing safety is not necessary to explain a missing-item procedure and instead encourages continued participation.

citations.quote: I personally love the eBay Money-back guarantee because it makes me feel very safe purchasing on the website.
it is important to reach out to your seller

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The branded appearance and customer-service role are consistent with the stated support purpose, not evidence of a deceptive promotion. The instructions concern a buyer's already-existing order and include conditional checks before escalation. The safety comment is an opinion, while the cited request process does not show a general reward, payment solicitation, or successful recovery.
